Building menus and content

Seven steps drawn from the redo of the Tracy Apple navigation, plus a table of T4 capabilities read straight from the plugin code and the demo page matrix derived from it.

Fifteen questions have answers (last section of the page). The next step is to build to the matrix in the T4 capabilities section, and only then wire the workflow into SKILL.md as a phase.

T4 capabilities, read from the plugin code

Not guessed from documentation: the tables below come from src/t4/Document/Template.php, themes/base/params/*.xml and the renderers in html/layouts/t4/.

A column can hold seven kinds of content

typewhat it isin use
componentwhere Joomla draws the current viewyes
positionsa position, holding several modulesyes
blocka file in html/layouts/t4/block/ — currently only header-1, header-2yes
elementlogo · masthead · megamenu · megamenu-toggle · offcanvas-toggleyes
moduleone specific module by id, not through a positionnot yet
rowa row nested in a column — a grid within a gridnot yet
spaceran empty placeholder columnnot yet

Each row has seventeen options

container · cols · padding and margin per each of five breakpoints · sticky · palettes · overlay + overlay_type · background image (repeat / size / attachment / position) · background video (mp4 / webm / ogg + poster image) · opacity · extra_class. Each column adds col and five variants xl/lg/md/sm/xs, plus hidden_* for each size.

Navigation is its own profile, not a layout

This is the easiest thing to miss: megamenu and off-canvas effects live in etc/navigation/*.json, so demoing them means creating several navigation profiles and attaching each one to a template style.

SettingValid valuesIn use
megamenu effectfading · slide · zoom · elastic · flipping1 / 5
off-canvas effectleft · left-reveal · left-push1 / 3
off-canvas menudef · drill · always-show1 / 3
megamenu columnitems · module · position3 / 3
mobile switch breakpointsm · md · lg · xl1 / 4

00

Take inventory before deciding

Open no admin page before knowing what the site has. Without this table every choice in the later steps is a guess.

Count by machine, don't estimate

  • Menu tree: menutype, level, view, template style of each item
  • Layout profiles in etc/layout/*.json — and which columns each profile declares
  • Positions: declared in templateDetails.xml versus positions that have modules
  • ACM blocks present in acm/ and the number of styles per block
  • Categories + the number of published articles in each
  • Content outside com_content: contact, newsfeed, tag, user, banner

Trap already hit: the template had a sidebar layout, a style attached to it, the position declared and a module sitting in that position — but the module pointed to a category with 0 articles. An empty module outputs nothing, T4 drops a column with no output, and the whole layout vanishes. No error, no empty column.

So the inventory must ask two questions for each position: is there a module, and does the module have content.

01

Choose the shape of the site

One question decides everything: is the person opening the site for the first time a customer of the company, or someone weighing whether to buy the template?

Settle before building

  • 5–6 top-level items, no more. Name them after what people need to do, not after how it was built
  • The minimum page set: About · Product · Service · Team · Contact · Blog · Pricing
  • Each top-level item carries a different proof of capability — if two items prove the same thing, merge them
  • No item is named “Pages”, “Demo”, “Megamenu”, “Elements”

Trap already hit: the old menu had 52 items, of which 17 under “Megamenu” were copies of Design + Pages + Blog, and “Pages” was a basket of 20 unrelated things. Reading the menu aloud did not sound like any company.

02

Assign a layout to each page

Layouts are what a template buyer looks at to learn what the template can do. Every profile must have at least one real page using it.

Allocation table

  • Full width — home page, Product, Pricing, landing pages
  • Right sidebar — wide detail pages (one article, one contact, one tag). Not list pages: a listing already fills the width with its own items
  • Left sidebar — the news / magazine area, where the navigation column stands before the content
  • No sidebar — single articles, documentation pages

Rules

  • A single article is always a reading column, whatever layout the menu item declares
  • A page whose body is only {loadposition} is a built page, not prose — it keeps the full width
gate: layout-scan over the whole pages.txt
03

Assign blocks to each page

The goal is that each kind of presentation appears at least once, and no page repeats exactly another page's set of blocks.

Cover every form

  • list · card · grid · carousel · accordion · tabs · timeline · statistics · quote
  • Each block used at least once; a block with only one style goes on the backlog for a second style
  • A page built from blocks does not show the article title and meta line — it is a page, not an article

Trap already hit: ACM params are stored flat; only repeating fieldsets (slides, quotes) nest. Nest by mistake and the block silently falls back to its sample content, and the page looks “right” until someone reads the text.

04

Rewrite the names

The most-skipped step, and the one that decides whether the site reads like a company or like a demo set.

The test

  • Read the whole menu aloud. If you hear the name of a template feature, change it
  • Item name = what the customer needs, not what the template can do
  • Sample content must change too: the text in blocks is a real company's text, not “Style 1 heading”
Demo nameWebsite nameWhy
List layoutAll articles“layout” is the builder's word
All categoriesTopicscategory is the CMS's word
Style guideDesign systemthe real name of what is on show
Single contactTalk to sales“single” is a view name
Single tagBrowse by tagsays what the reader does
Home 2Home — varianta sequence number says nothing
LandingCampaign pagesays the purpose
FAQHelp centrebroader, more accurate
05

Build the menu in Joomla

Four things Joomla does not keep in sync by itself. Each one broke a build today.

  • #__menu has no ordering column — the order is lft
  • The nested set must be renumbered by hand after every insert or parent change: walk the tree by parent_id, write lft/rgt/level
  • path does not follow parent_id — it must be recomputed from the alias chain, otherwise the old URL 404s while the item looks perfect
  • A megamenu column of type position reads name, not position

Pages that need a route but must not show

  • Don't hide the parent item to conceal a branch: Joomla still renders the child items (they attach to the nearest top-level item) while the router rejects their paths — the site prints links and then 404s on them itself
  • The right way: move them to a second menutype, still published, rendered by no module
gates: nav-scan · link-scan
06

Sync every copy of the menu

The main menu is not the only place the site states its structure. Fixing the menu and forgetting the copies leaves the site contradicting itself.

List to check

  • Footer nav — if it is a hand-written mod_custom it does not update itself. This is the most often forgotten copy
  • Off-canvas — uses mod_menu so it follows automatically, but check the second level again
  • Modules inside megamenu panels — their content points to categories, and a category may just have changed
  • Hard links in ACM blocks and in articles — CTA buttons, “read more”, hand-made breadcrumbs
  • Colophon / legal in the footer — often mentions the names of renamed pages

Trap already hit: after the new menu was built, the footer still printed three columns Design · Pages · Account — a structure the header had dropped. The links still worked because they use Itemid, so no gate reported it; only a human eye saw it.

07

Let the machine check, then look

This order matters: measure first to know what is wrong, look afterwards to know whether it is right.

Run everything, not a few pages

  • link-scan — crawls from /, following every link the site prints
  • nav-scan — rendered menu, megamenu panels, sidebar columns, sticky bar, header block height
  • layout-scan — the whole pages.txt, and pages.txt must be updated to the new menu
  • contrast-audit · token-scan — on the new pages

Trap already hit: the gate was right but was not run. After a fix round I ran only the two pages I had open, while pages.txt had 32 pages — and the defect was on the third. Sweeping the whole list takes about 90 seconds.

GatesBuild all five

Five gates to write

  • footer matches menu — every footer link must point to a published menu item, and the groups must match the top-level item names
  • no demo names — a list of words banned in menu item names: layout, single, style 1, demo, page 2…
  • every layout profile has a page using it — read etc/layout/*.json, cross-check template styles and menu items
  • every ACM block is used at least once — read acm/, cross-check published modules
  • every category in the menu has ≥ 9 articles — a three-article listing looks like an unfinished site

Deferred to phase 2

  • E-commerce · booking · multi-step forms (need extensions outside T4)
  • Multilingual: menus, content, and the language switcher in the header
